change.author: Eunjae Lee

findings.title: Public auth/filter conditions are returned without outer parentheses
findings.body: `getAuthorizationConditions()` and `getFilterConditions()` are public, and the org/team auth fragment is `(A) OR (B)` and the event-type filter is `(x) OR (y)`, both with no outer parentheses. `getBaseConditions` wraps each one, so it is correct. A caller that interpolates the fragment directly, for example ``WHERE ${auth} AND "createdAt" > ...``, gets `(A) OR (B) AND ...` because AND binds tighter than OR. That would let bookings outside the authorised scope through, since the auth fragment is the access-control boundary. Consider wrapping the final result of `buildOrgAuthorizationCondition`, `buildTeamAuthorizationCondition` and the event-type filter in `( ... )`, or making only `getBaseConditions` public. The same applies to lines 119-122, 204-207 and 106. The tests assert the unwrapped shape, so they would need updating too. I found no other callers in the repository, so this is a robustness point rather than a bug today.

findings.title: Loose public options type removes compile-time check for the team scope
findings.body: `InsightsBookingServicePublicOptions` makes `teamId` optional for every scope, so `scope: "team"` without `teamId` now compiles. Zod then rejects it at runtime and the service silently returns `1=0`, an empty result with no error. The old constructor took the discriminated union type, which caught this at compile time. A discriminated union type (or `z.input` of the schema) would keep the check. If the loose type is deliberate, for example to accept tRPC input, a comment saying so would help.

findings.title: Dead branches in getBaseConditions
findings.body: `getAuthorizationConditions()` always returns a `Prisma.Sql`, which is always truthy. So the `else if (filterConditions)` and `else` branches that return `filterConditions` or `NOTHING_CONDITION` can never run. Simplify to `return filterConditions ? Prisma.sql`(${auth}) AND (${filterConditions})` : auth`.

findings.title: Lost coverage: caching tests removed, and the new SQL paths are barely run against the database
findings.body: The Caching tests were deleted. The `cachedAuthConditions` and `cachedFilterConditions` logic still exists in the service, so it is now untested. Only the user scope is executed against the DB, in the `getBaseConditions` test. The org and team fragments with `ANY(array)` and the `isTeamBooking` OR-combination are checked only by `toEqual` on the `Sql` object. That does not show the SQL is valid or returns the right rows, for example when the array parameter is bound as `int[]`. There is also no test for `getBaseConditions` when the user is not an owner or admin (`1=0`), or for the team scope with no members (the new omitted-branch case).

contracts.action: InsightsBookingService now builds Prisma.sql fragments and exposes getBaseConditions instead of running findMany
contracts.equivalent_path: Previous findMany, which AND-ed auth and filter Prisma where-inputs into a bookingTimeStatusDenormalized.findMany call
contracts.before_after: Before, the service executed the query and merged the conditions into the caller's `where`. Now it returns a Sql fragment `(auth) AND (filter)` and the caller embeds it in its own $queryRaw. Not-owner and invalid-options cases still give a match-nothing condition (`1=0` instead of `id = -1`). The auth fragment is the same logical predicate as before. The one structural change is that empty `userId IN []` branches are dropped.
contracts.visible_effect: No UI change in this part. Nothing else in the repository calls the service, so the findMany removal breaks no caller.
contracts.failure_mode: If a caller interpolates getAuthorizationConditions or getFilterConditions directly (not through getBaseConditions), OR precedence is not protected. See the finding on line 171. Invalid options or a non-admin user give an empty result silently.

summary: The conversion from Prisma where-inputs to Prisma.sql fragments looks logically equivalent, and the test expectations match the built SQL. Four low-severity points remain. The public condition getters return fragments without outer parentheses, so a direct caller could get wrong AND/OR precedence on the auth fragment. The public options type is looser than the schema. Some branches in `getBaseConditions` are dead. The caching tests were dropped and the org and team SQL is not run against the database.
